Jane — thanks for the clarity. To keep procurement moving, here's a proposed carveout we can put in the SOW for your Dedicated cluster (draft, subject to legal/product review):

1) Initial-frame (contract-level): Redwood will guarantee the first data frame will be delivered within 350ms p95 for requests with prompt+expected_output <= 512 tokens when routed to Acme's Dedicated pool. Measurement is from request receipt at Redwood's API gateway to first data chunk transmitted.

2) Sustained token-rate (contract-level): For streaming sessions longer than 10s, Redwood will maintain a sustained rate >= 70 tokens/sec p50 and >= 50 tokens/sec p95 measured over a 30s sliding window. Bursts up to 220 tokens/sec for up to 45s are permitted for short peak events.

3) Failure modes and remediation: If p95 initial-frame exceeds 350ms or sustained p95 token-rate falls below 50 tokens/sec for more than 3 consecutive 5-minute windows, Redwood will trigger an incident, notify Acme, and apply service credit of 5% monthly invoice for each qualifying breach (capped at 30% per month).

4) Operational controls: Acme may request routing to a ‘low-latency’ subpool (subject to capacity commit). Redwood will provide trace IDs, a real-time dashboard link, and a retention window of 90 days for logs tied to this SLO.
